Evaluation on 01/21/2024

Subjective:
The patient is a 72-year-old male presenting for follow-up of prior laboratory testing and chest CT. Care was established recently after relocating from another region earlier in November. He reports feeling well and denies chest pain or palpitations.

Objective:
Vital signs: Blood pressure 123/63 (left arm, seated), pulse 80, respiratory rate 16, height 1.727 m (5'8"), weight 74.8 kg (165 lb), SpO2 99%, BMI 25.09.
General: Alert, oriented, well nourished, no acute distress.
Eyes: Conjunctiva normal.
Head: Normocephalic, atraumatic.
Neck: Supple.
Respiratory: Non-labored breathing.
Neurologic: Awake, oriented to person, place, time, and situation.
Psychiatric: Cooperative, mood and affect appropriate.

Mental health screening:
PHQ-9 (12/04/2023): Item 1 score 0 (no loss of interest), Item 2 score 0 (no depressed mood).
GAD-7: No data available.

Diagnostics and results:
- Colonoscopy (10/14/2022): Abnormal.
- Cardiopulmonary data (01/15/2024): Heart rate 68; RR 876; P-R interval 189; P axis 58; QRS duration 103; QT interval 389; QTc 416; QRS axis 46; T-wave axis 30. ECG impression: Otherwise normal ECG; sinus rhythm; minimal ST elevation in anterior leads.
- Hospital outpatient labs (01/05/2024):
  Urine: Albumin <7; creatinine 31.90; albumin/creatinine ratio not calculable.
  Glycemic: Hemoglobin A1c 6.2 (H).
  Lipids: Total cholesterol 124; triglycerides 74; HDL 51; direct LDL 63; cholesterol/HDL ratio 2.4; non-HDL 73.
  Electrolytes/chemistry: Sodium 140; potassium 4.4; chloride 103; CO2 28; anion gap 9; fasting: No; glucose 87.
  Renal: Creatinine 0.73; eGFR 97; BUN 18.
  Calcium: 10.1.
  Liver/proteins: Total protein 7.3; albumin 4.4; total bilirubin 0.3; alkaline phosphatase 55; AST 32; ALT 37; globulin 2.9.
  Endocrine/other: TSH 0.79; PSA 1.0.
  CBC: WBC 5.4; RBC 4.67; hemoglobin 14.6; hematocrit 44.4; MCV 95.1; MCH 31.3; MCHC 32.9; RDW 12.5; platelets 228.
  Differential: Neutrophils 53.6% (absolute 2.91); lymphocytes 32.5% (absolute 1.77); monocytes 9.9% (absolute 0.54); eosinophils 2.9% (absolute 0.16); basophils 0.9% (absolute 0.05); immature granulocytes 0.2% (absolute 0.01); nRBC 0.00 (0.0%).
- CT chest without contrast (12/18/2023):
  Clinical history: 72-year-old male with prior lung nodules; repeat imaging due; last check 05/17/2022; incidental left adrenal adenoma 1.4 cm previously noted.
  Comparison: None.
  Technique: Noncontrast chest CT performed. Radiation metrics: CTDIvol 10.18 (mGy); DLP 368 (mGy-cm).
  Findings: No devices. Thyroid with hypoattenuating nodules up to 1 cm. Lymph nodes: limited assessment without contrast; no supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal, or hilar adenopathy. Vascular: limited evaluation; aorta and main pulmonary artery diameters within normal limits; atherosclerotic calcifications of the aorta and branch vessels. Cardiac: mild coronary artery calcification; no pericardial effusion. Mediastinum: unremarkable on noncontrast imaging. Lungs: mild apical scarring; trace apical emphysema; scattered calcified granulomas. Small nodules include a 3 mm solid nodule in the left lower lobe (4:158), a 3 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe (4:176), and a 4 mm ground-glass nodule versus confluence of vessels in the posterior basal right lower lobe (4:261). Airways: moderate, diffuse bronchial wall thickening with mild central airway irregularity. Pleura: normal. Chest wall/spine: bilateral gynecomastia. Upper abdomen: left adrenal adenoma measuring 1.4 cm (5:365); hepatic calcified granuloma.
  Impression: (1) Several small pulmonary nodules up to 4 mm. Submission of prior external imaging for comparison is recommended; if unavailable, a repeat CT in 1 year can be considered based on risk factors. (2) Bronchial wall thickening and mild central airway irregularity consistent with chronic bronchitis.

Assessment and plan:
- Prediabetes: Hemoglobin A1c 6.2 within the prediabetic range. Advised dietary and lifestyle modification. Plan to repeat A1c in about 6 months; future A1c ordered.
- Pulmonary nodules: Multiple nodules <4 mm without prior comparison imaging. Plan to repeat chest CT on 12/17/2024; earlier if clinically indicated.
- Left adrenal gland adenoma: Incidental, 1.4 cm. Current labs are normal; blood pressure well controlled at home. Will repeat imaging in 1 year; sooner if needed. Offered referral to an adrenal tumor specialist.
- Onychomycosis: The patient declined both oral and topical therapy at this time.

The care plan was reviewed with the patient, and questions were answered.

Follow-up: 6 months, or earlier if concerns arise.

Encounter date: 12/04/2023

Reason for visit: establishing primary care and requesting medication refills; reports palpitations.

Current medications at presentation:
- Ezetimibe 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin (Lipitor) 10 mg nightly

- Montelukast (Singulair) 10 mg nightly

History of present illness:

  Clinical history: 72-year-old male with prior lung nodules; repeat imaging due; last check 05/17/2022; incidental left adrenal adenoma 1.4 cm previously noted.

Airways: moderate, diffuse bronchial wall thickening with mild central airway irregularity. Pleura: normal. Chest wall/spine: bilateral gynecomastia. Upper abdomen: left adrenal adenoma measuring 1.4 cm (5:365); hepatic calcified granuloma.
  Impression: (1) Several small pulmonary nodules up to 4 mm. Submission of prior external imaging for comparison is recommended; if unavailable, a repeat CT in 1 year can be considered based on risk factors. (2) Bronchial wall thickening and mild central airway irregularity consistent with chronic bronchitis.

- Prediabetes: Hemoglobin A1c 6.2 within the prediabetic range. Advised dietary and lifestyle modification. Plan to repeat A1c in about 6 months; future A1c ordered.

- Left adrenal gland adenoma: Incidental, 1.4 cm. Current labs are normal; blood pressure well controlled at home. Will repeat imaging in 1 year; sooner if needed. Offered referral to an adrenal tumor specialist.
- Onychomycosis: The patient declined both oral and topical therapy at this time.

args.content:
Adrenal Incidentaloma Assessment and Management Plan
Date/time of assessment: 2024-03-11 23:20
Endocrinology reviewer: Gabriel Ingram, MD (Practitioner/dr-gabriel-ingram)
Patient: MRN6756332150, 72-year-old man (DOB 1951-07-09)

Reason for review
CT imaging was flagged for an incidental left adrenal finding. I reviewed available EHR data, including demographics, problem list, medications, vitals, laboratory observations, procedures, and clinical note/imaging-report text available in DocumentReference resources.

Key data reviewed
1) Imaging documenting adrenal lesion
- CT chest without IV contrast, performed 12/18/2023, available in 01/21/2024 progress note:
  - Upper abdomen: left adrenal adenoma measuring 1.4 cm.
  - Clinical history states prior lung nodule surveillance imaging from 05/17/2022 and a previously noted incidental left adrenal adenoma 1.4 cm, but the outside comparison images/report were not available in the retrieved chart.
  - The 12/18/2023 report does not provide adrenal-specific characterization: no unenhanced Hounsfield units, homogeneity details, borders, dedicated adrenal measurements in 3 planes, contrast washout, or chemical-shift MRI data.
  - Other relevant CT findings: mild coronary artery calcification; aortic/branch-vessel atherosclerotic calcifications; several pulmonary nodules up to 4 mm; chronic bronchitis-type airway changes.
- Procedures show an “IMAGING” entry dated 03/02/2024, but I could not retrieve a corresponding report or clinical note after 01/21/2024 from available DocumentReference searches. Therefore, management is based on the available adrenal documentation above and the current flagged incidentaloma context.

2) Diagnoses / comorbidities relevant to adrenal evaluation
- Active adrenal-related problem entries: adrenal nodule/other specified adrenal disorder/left adrenal adenoma.
- Cardiometabolic/cardiovascular: essential hypertension; hyperlipidemia by clinical note; positive/abnormal heart CT score by clinical note; mild coronary/aortic atherosclerotic calcification on CT; heart palpitations; supraventricular tachycardia on problem list; family history of CAD by clinical note; prediabetes.
- Other: pulmonary nodules, asthma, BPH, insomnia, onychomycosis.
- Tobacco status: never smoker.

3) Current medications
- Amlodipine 2.5 mg daily.
- Irbesartan 75 mg nightly.
- Atorvastatin 10 mg nightly.
- Ezetimibe 10 mg daily.
- Montelukast 10 mg daily/nightly.
- Zolpidem 5 mg at bedtime as needed.
No mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, diuretic, beta blocker, oral estrogen, or chronic glucocorticoid was found in active medication orders.

4) Blood pressure control
- 12/04/2023 vitals: initial BP 177/70, repeat 134/69; note-documented visit BP 131/68.
- 01/21/2024 vitals: BP 145/69 then 124/60; note-documented visit BP 123/63.
- Primary care notes state home BPs reportedly at target/well controlled.
Overall: hypertension appears generally controlled on two agents, but adrenal incidentaloma plus hypertension still warrants primary aldosteronism screening even with normal potassium.

5) Pertinent labs
- 01/05/2024 chemistry observations: sodium 136.85 mmol/L, potassium 4.48 mmol/L, chloride 98.16 mmol/L, CO2 28.42 mmol/L, BUN 18.08 mg/dL, creatinine 0.74 mg/dL, glucose 84.55 mg/dL, calcium 10.5 mg/dL.
- 01/21/2024 note summary of 01/05/2024 labs: creatinine 0.73, eGFR 97, potassium 4.4, sodium 140, glucose 87, calcium 10.1, normal LFTs, TSH 0.79, CBC unremarkable.
- A1c 6.2% on 01/05/2024, consistent with prediabetes.
Interpretation: renal function is adequate for contrast CT if no interval change; potassium is normal; no biochemical evidence of hypokalemia. Borderline calcium elevation in discrete lab observation should be rechecked with the BMP and pursued if persistent.

Assessment
- Small left adrenal incidentaloma, reported as a 1.4 cm adenoma on a noncontrast chest CT, but adrenal-specific imaging criteria are incomplete. Although the term “adenoma” is used and the lesion may have been known previously, the available report does not document HU <=10, lipid-rich appearance, washout, or stability by actual comparison. Dedicated adrenal characterization is therefore appropriate.
- Hormonal evaluation is indicated despite small size:
  1. Screen for autonomous cortisol secretion in all adrenal incidentalomas. This is particularly important here because the patient has hypertension, prediabetes, and cardiovascular disease risk/coronary calcification.
  2. Screen for pheochromocytoma because unenhanced HU is not documented and the patient has palpitations/SVT history. If the forthcoming dedicated noncontrast CT documents a homogeneous lesion with HU <=10, pheochromocytoma becomes much less likely, but current data are insufficient to omit testing.
  3. Screen for primary aldosteronism because he has hypertension plus an adrenal mass, even though potassium is normal.
- No current indication for sex-steroid testing or adrenal carcinoma marker testing because lesion is small (1.4 cm) and the available report does not describe suspicious imaging features or virilization/feminization. This will be reconsidered if adrenal-protocol imaging shows heterogeneity, irregular margins, high HU, growth, or size >=4 cm.

Orders placed
1) 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test
- MedicationRequest 212157: dexamethasone 1 mg tablet, take once at 11 PM to midnight the night before testing.
- ServiceRequest 212158: 8 AM serum cortisol after 1 mg overnight dexamethasone.
- ServiceRequest 212159: serum dexamethasone level drawn concurrently to confirm adequate dexamethasone exposure.
Patient instructions: Take dexamethasone 1 mg by mouth between 11 PM and midnight. Present to the lab at 8 AM the next morning for cortisol and dexamethasone levels. Avoid taking unreported steroid medications or supplements; notify the team if using glucocorticoid injections, steroid creams in high dose, anticonvulsants, rifampin, azole antifungals, ritonavir/cobicistat, or other strong CYP3A4 modifiers, because they can affect test interpretation.

2) Pheochromocytoma screen
- ServiceRequest 212160: plasma free fractionated metanephrines.
Patient instructions: Preferred collection is fasting, morning if feasible. Avoid caffeine, nicotine, decongestants/sympathomimetics, and vigorous exercise for 24 hours before the draw. Rest supine in a quiet room for 20-30 minutes before blood draw. If the specimen is collected seated and results are only mildly elevated, repeat supine testing may be needed before labeling the result abnormal.

3) Primary aldosteronism screen
- ServiceRequest 212161: plasma aldosterone, renin activity/concentration, and aldosterone-renin ratio.
Patient instructions: Morning draw. Maintain usual sodium intake; do not restrict salt before testing. Potassium should be normal at the time of testing. Ideally collect after being out of bed for at least 2 hours and seated for 5-15 minutes. Continue current antihypertensives for the initial screen for safety. Note: irbesartan can raise renin and may cause a false-negative ARR; if ARR is negative but suspicion remains, repeat testing after holding ARB 2-4 weeks with substitute agents that minimally affect ARR (e.g., verapamil SR, hydralazine, or alpha blocker) if clinically safe.

4) Chemistry / renal function
- ServiceRequest 212162: basic metabolic panel to recheck sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, creatinine/eGFR, glucose, and calcium with the hormonal workup and before contrast imaging.

5) Adrenal mass characterization imaging
- ServiceRequest 212163: CT abdomen without and with IV contrast, adrenal protocol with washout, requested within 1-2 months; target occurrence 2024-04-15.
Radiology request: characterize 1.4 cm left adrenal lesion; report noncontrast HU, size in 3 dimensions, homogeneity, margins, absolute and relative washout if contrast/washout performed, and contralateral adrenal appearance; compare with any outside 05/17/2022 imaging and any 03/02/2024 imaging if available.

Contingency plan
1) If post-dexamethasone cortisol <=1.8 mcg/dL with adequate dexamethasone level:
- Autonomous cortisol secretion is excluded; no cortisol-directed therapy needed unless new clinical features develop.

2) If post-dexamethasone cortisol >1.8 mcg/dL:
- Confirm adequate dexamethasone level and absence of interfering medications/nonadherence.
- Repeat/confirm testing as appropriate and obtain morning ACTH +/- DHEA-S to establish ACTH-independence.
- Assess cortisol-related comorbidities: BP, A1c/glucose, lipids, weight, osteoporosis/fracture risk, and cardiovascular risk.
- If mild autonomous cortisol secretion is confirmed, discuss at adrenal multidisciplinary conference if comorbidities are worsening or difficult to control; consider adrenalectomy vs conservative management based on degree of cortisol autonomy, age, surgical risk, patient preference, and imaging phenotype.
- If overt Cushing syndrome biochemistry or symptoms emerge, expedite endocrine follow-up and adrenal surgery evaluation after full localization/staging.

3) If plasma metanephrines are elevated:
- If >3 times upper limit of normal or clearly abnormal under appropriate collection conditions, treat as likely pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma: urgent endocrine follow-up, avoid adrenal biopsy and nonurgent invasive procedures until evaluated, obtain dedicated anatomic/functional imaging as indicated, and refer for adrenal surgery with preoperative alpha blockade.
- If mild elevation, review collection posture, stress, medications, renal function, and repeat supine plasma metanephrines or 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines before definitive diagnosis.

4) If ARR is positive:
- Confirm potassium is normal and interpret in context of irbesartan/amlodipine.
- Repeat ARR with medication adjustment if needed; proceed to confirmatory testing for primary aldosteronism unless phenotype is unequivocal.
- If confirmed, determine laterality with adrenal-protocol imaging and usually adrenal venous sampling if surgery is considered; unilateral disease may be treated with adrenalectomy, bilateral disease or nonsurgical preference with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist therapy.

5) Imaging results:
- If homogeneous, lipid-rich adenoma with HU <=10 and size remains <4 cm without concerning features: no surgery; additional imaging may not be needed if stability/benignity is clear, though final decision will incorporate prior outside comparison.
- If HU 11-20, indeterminate washout, or incomplete characterization: consider MRI chemical-shift imaging or repeat interval imaging per adrenal tumor board/radiology recommendation.
- If size >=4 cm, HU >20, heterogeneous/irregular lesion, necrosis/hemorrhage, local invasion, or significant growth (>20% and at least 5 mm increase, or clinically meaningful interval growth): refer to adrenal multidisciplinary tumor board and endocrine surgery; consider malignancy workup.
- Adrenal biopsy is not indicated for routine incidentaloma evaluation and must not be performed until pheochromocytoma is excluded; consider only if there is a known extra-adrenal malignancy and the result would change management.

6) BMP/calcium:
- If potassium is low, repeat ARR interpretation should account for hypokalemia and potassium should be corrected before repeat testing.
- If calcium remains elevated, repeat calcium with albumin and consider PTH/25-OH vitamin D evaluation, independent of adrenal incidentaloma workup.

Follow-up
- Review biochemical results as they return; prioritize urgent contact for markedly abnormal metanephrines or severe hypokalemia.
- Review adrenal protocol CT when completed, ideally by mid-April 2024, and decide whether surveillance, additional imaging, adrenal tumor board discussion, or surgery referral is needed.
- Coordinate with primary care/cardiology regarding BP, prediabetes, lipid/coronary risk, and palpitations/SVT while endocrine workup is pending.
